## Unified API

Send operation input as a JSON object to `POST /api/v1/integrations/git/{operation}`. Use `Content-Type: application/json` and `Authorization: Bearer zint_...` with your app token. The token is scoped to one connection and category.

Read `GET /api/v1/integrations/git/capabilities` with the same token. It returns an object keyed by operation, each containing `support` and a `fields` map. It does not use the operation response envelope.

Successful operations return HTTP 200 with `{support, warnings, data}`. `support` is `native` or `emulated`. `warnings` is an array of `{code, field}` objects, empty when nothing was dropped. `data` has the operation's response fields below. Unknown input fields are rejected.

| Operation | Summary | Provider support |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `create_issue` | Create an issue with optional labels. | Gitea / Forgejo: native; GitHub: native |
| `get_file` | Read a file at a branch, tag, or commit. | Gitea / Forgejo: native; GitHub: native |
| `get_readme` | Read the repository README. | Gitea / Forgejo: emulated; GitHub: native |
| `get_repo` | Read repository details. | Gitea / Forgejo: native; GitHub: native |
| `list_branches` | List repository branches. | Gitea / Forgejo: native; GitHub: native |
| `list_issues` | List issues without pull requests. | Gitea / Forgejo: native; GitHub: native |
| `list_repos` | List repositories for an owner. | Gitea / Forgejo: native; GitHub: native |
| `search_code` | Search repository code. | Gitea / Forgejo: unsupported; GitHub: native |

### `create_issue`

Create an issue with optional labels.

Input fields:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `body` | string | No | Issue body; defaults to empty. |
| `labels` | array of string | No | Non-empty label names. Gitea and Forgejo require existing repository labels. |
| `owner` | string | Yes | Repository owner; a non-empty path segment. |
| `repo` | string | Yes | Repository name; a non-empty path segment. |
| `title` | string | Yes | Non-empty issue title. |

Response fields in `data`:

| Name | Type |
| --- | --- |
| `author` | string |
| `body` | string |
| `labels` | array of string |
| `number` | integer |
| `state` | string |
| `title` | string |
| `url` | string |

### `get_file`

Read a file at a branch, tag, or commit.

Input fields:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `owner` | string | Yes | Repository owner; a non-empty path segment. |

| `ref` | string | No | Branch, tag, or commit; defaults to the repository default branch. |
| `repo` | string | Yes | Repository name; a non-empty path segment. |

Response fields in `data`:

| Name | Type |

| `content` | string |
| `encoding` | string |
| `path` | string |
| `ref` | string |
| `size` | integer |

### Run a request

Set your app token before running this example.

```bash
export INTEGRATIONS_URL='https://app.zenith.hosting/api/v1/integrations'
read -r -s -p 'App token: ' GIT_TOKEN
printf '\n'
export GIT_TOKEN
curl --fail-with-body --silent --show-error \
  "$INTEGRATIONS_URL/git/capabilities" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GIT_TOKEN"
curl --fail-with-body --silent --show-error \
  "$INTEGRATIONS_URL/git/list_repos" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GIT_TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"owner":"zenith-hosting"}'
```

### Errors and strict mode

Integration errors return `{code, operation, provider}` with optional `field`, `message`, and `retry_after`. Authentication failures return only `{"code":"unauthorized"}` and a `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` header. Handle errors by `code`.

| Code | HTTP status | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `field_unsupported` | 422 | Strict mode rejected an unsupported input field before calling the provider. |
| `invalid_input` | 400 | Invalid JSON, fields, values, or degradation mode. |
| `not_found` | 404 | The requested resource was not found. |
| `operation_emulated` | 501 | Strict mode rejected an emulated operation. |
| `operation_unsupported` | 501 | The provider does not support this operation. |
| `provider_auth` | 424 | Provider credentials failed; reconnect the provider. |
| `provider_rate_limited` | 429 | Provider rate limit reached; respect the Retry-After header when present. |
| `provider_unavailable` | 502 | Provider failure or invalid response; retry later. |
| `unauthorized` | 401 | Missing, expired, revoked, or incorrectly scoped app token. |

Omit `Zenith-Degrade` or set it to `best-effort` to allow emulation. Dropped input fields produce `field_dropped` warnings. Send `Zenith-Degrade: strict` to reject emulation and unsupported input fields before the provider call. Unsupported operations fail in both modes.

## Provider support

`native` calls the provider directly. `emulated` combines native operations. `unsupported` cannot run. Support describes the adapter; provider permissions and resource availability still apply.

| Operation | Gitea / Forgejo | GitHub |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `create_issue` | native | native |
| `get_file` | native | native |
| `get_readme` | emulated | native |
| `get_repo` | native | native |
| `list_branches` | native | native |
| `list_issues` | native | native |
| `list_repos` | native | native |
| `search_code` | unsupported | native |

### Field support

These fields have explicit capability declarations. Check them before relying on invitations, labels, or pagination. Unsupported input fields are dropped in best-effort mode; field support on read operations also describes what the provider can return.

| Operation | Field | Gitea / Forgejo | GitHub |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `create_issue` | `labels` | native | native |

## Setup

<Visibility for="humans">

<Steps>
<Step title="Connect a provider">
Open [Settings > Integrations](https://app.zenith.hosting/settings/integrations) in the Zenith dashboard. Choose a provider and enter its connection fields below.
</Step>
<Step title="Create an app token">
Create a token for your app on that connection. Copy it into the app's token input in the deployment Credentials panel.
</Step>
</Steps>

</Visibility>

Connection fields:

### Gitea / Forgejo

| Field | Label | Required | Secret |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | API URL | Yes | No |
| `token` | Token | No | Yes |

### GitHub

| Field | Label | Required | Secret |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `token` | Token | No | Yes |

### Declare app environment inputs

Merge this declaration into `zenith-compose.yml`. Replace `app` with the service that calls the API. See the [environment reference](/content/zenith-compose-reference#env).

```yaml zenith-compose.yml
x-zenith:
  env:
    INTEGRATIONS_URL:
      input:
        label: Integrations URL
        default: https://app.zenith.hosting/api/v1/integrations
      services:
        - app
    GIT_TOKEN:
      input:
        label: Git token
        secret: true
      services:
        - app
```

The token has no default. Leave `input.required` unset so submission validation can run before the owner supplies it. Your app must handle a missing token and enable the integration after the owner configures it. These inputs use the published runtime contract; the current CLI preview policy does not accept `x-zenith.env`. For an authorized preview, follow the preview guide's local environment workflow and report any validation limit.

Then use the zenith-integrations skill to wire the app to the

Call POST $INTEGRATIONS_URL/git/{operation} with JSON input.
Handle support, field_dropped warnings, typed errors,
Retry-After and a missing token. Send Zenith-Degrade: strict
when a dropped field or emulation would be incorrect.
Run the app's tests and NO_COLOR=1 zenith check after Compose
changes. Report preview-policy limits separately from
published runtime support.
With an authorized preview and token, verify a native and an
emulated operation where available, strict rejection and
visible warnings. Check side effects of authorized writes and
report anything unverified.
Do not invent tokens, log secrets, connect accounts, deploy or
publish without authorization for that action.
